criteria.name: netlink_persist_behavior
criteria.description: Default netlink path keeps -persist resident: dead-conn timeout is applied (explicit or sensible default), process monitors link-dead events, reconnects with backoff, and reconfigures sockets into the kernel instead of exiting right after connect.
criteria.reasoning: The code implements a persistent mode for netlink-configured devices that meets all the required criteria. It applies a dead-conn timeout (either explicit via -T/--dead-timeout or a sensible default of 30 seconds when persisting). The process monitors link-dead events via the 'nbd_mc_group' multicast group using netlink sockets. Upon receiving a link-dead notification, it reconnects to the server with exponential backoff (starting at 1 second, max 180 seconds) and reconfigures the new sockets into the kernel using NBD_CMD_RECONFIGURE rather than exiting. This allows queued I/O to be retried over the new connections.

criteria.name: fix_locality
criteria.description: Changes stay around nbd-client netlink/persist wiring; ioctl legacy path is not ripped out; no unrelated churn or cheat-by-tests.
criteria.reasoning: The changes are highly focused on the netlink/persist functionality. The ioctl legacy path remains fully intact and is used when netlink is disabled. The implementation adds netlink-specific functions (netlink_configure, netlink_disconnect, netlink_check_conn, netlink_persist, etc.) without modifying unrelated code paths. There's no unnecessary churn - the changes are precisely what's needed to implement proper persistence with netlink, including handling dead connection timeouts, monitoring link events, reconnecting with backoff, and reconfiguring sockets. The code maintains clear separation between netlink and legacy ioctl paths.
